paragraphs: Training a model to repair code requires examples of broken programs and their fixes. This paper creates those examples through self-play: one model alternates between introducing bugs and repairing them, using unit tests to check the results. As its repair ability improves, its bug-generation role produces harder challenges, creating an automatic training curriculum.

The difficulty is that passing tests does not establish whether generated bugs resemble practical programming mistakes. The authors find that unrestricted self-play can improve repair of its own generated bugs while worsening repair of real-world bugs. Anchored Self Play addresses this drift with a small reference collection: code-embedding similarity rewards guide bug generation, and reference bugs also enter repair training.

The authors introduce BugSourceBench to cover human bugs, model-generated errors, and human edits of buggy model code. Across these sources, anchored training achieves the best reported fix rates. Its average improvement over standard self-play is 25% relative, or 7.2 percentage points absolute, showing that grounding the curriculum in reference bugs improves its practical relevance.
icml-2026-anchored-self-play-for-code-re.tldr: Anchoring code-repair self-play to reference bugs reduces curriculum drift and improves repair across human- and model-generated bug sources.

paragraphs: This paper studies fair allocation when indivisible goods arrive one at a time and each assignment is permanent. It focuses on proportionality up to one good, called PROP1, a fairness criterion that tolerates a one-item shortfall. The question is whether an online allocation procedure can approximately satisfy this criterion despite having to act before seeing future goods.

The authors first show that three natural greedy rules cannot guarantee any multiplicative PROP1 approximation against an adversary that adapts to the allocation process. They then examine less demanding conditions. Against a non-adaptive adversary, uniform random allocation achieves an approximation with high probability. Its guarantee is essentially tight for that approach, and sufficiently small item values allow near-PROP1 allocations with high probability.

A further algorithm uses predictions of maximum item values to obtain robust PROP1 approximation guarantees, with graceful degradation under one-sided prediction errors. These predictions have specific rather than universal power: even perfect maximum-value predictions do not make EF1, MMS, or PROPX approximable in the studied setting.
icml-2026-approximate-proportionality-in.tldr: Online PROP1 fairness admits useful approximation guarantees under non-adaptive arrivals or maximum-item-value predictions, despite failures of natural greedy rules.

paragraphs: Most forecasting models map past observations directly to a future target interval. This paper considers a longer structure: the history, the target, and the trajectory after that target. That later continuation can provide useful structural information, but its actual values are unavailable when a forecast must be made. The approach therefore seeks an approximate continuation proxy.

KUP-BI obtains continuation-style knowledge from a historical library containing training trajectories only. It integrates this knowledge into standard forecasting models through two streams: one represents the current input, and the other represents the continuation proxy. A lightweight feature-level gate combines them, allowing the forecast to draw on typical continuation patterns represented in the training data.

The distinction between a proxy and the actual future is central to the method. KUP-BI adds no information beyond the training trajectories; it organizes existing information into a structural guide for forecasting. Across six public datasets, the authors report consistent improvements to state-of-the-art forecasting models with small additional overhead, supporting this use of historical continuation patterns.
icml-2026-beyond-extrapolation-knowledge.tldr: KUP-BI improves forecasting by combining current history with a continuation proxy derived exclusively from training trajectories.

paragraphs: Long-horizon goal-conditioned reinforcement learning requires actions that contribute to an eventual objective across many steps. In the offline setting, the policy learns from existing data. Hierarchical approaches help by introducing intermediate goals, but the paper identifies structural limitations in designs that use separate high- and low-level networks and predict just one intermediate subgoal.

Chain-of-Goals Hierarchical Policy, or CoGHP, instead produces a sequence within one architecture. Starting from the current state and final goal, it generates latent subgoals one after another and then predicts a primitive action. Each subgoal conditions the predictions that follow, so intermediate representations become successive planning steps rather than a single bridge between the present state and final destination.

An MLP-Mixer backbone supports communication among the tokens representing state, goal, subgoals, and action. This gives the unified policy a way to capture their structural relationships efficiently. On challenging navigation and manipulation benchmarks, CoGHP consistently outperforms strong offline baselines. The findings support sequential subgoal generation as a useful structure for the evaluated long-horizon tasks.
icml-2026-chain-of-goals-hierarchical-po.tldr: CoGHP improves long-horizon offline control by generating a chain of latent subgoals and an action within one sequential policy.

paragraphs: Graph kernels describe relationships between graph nodes, and graph random features approximate computations involving those kernels. Existing graph random features can struggle to represent relationships between distant nodes. Capturing those relationships through longer random walks also creates a computational burden, because sampling a long walk involves sequential work along its path.

The proposed refined graph random features, GRFs++, use walk stitching to concatenate several shorter walks while preserving unbiasedness. This retains the approximation quality associated with longer walks but changes how the computation is organized. Short walks can be computed in parallel and combined through matrix multiplication, replacing inefficient sequential sampling with a more efficient computational structure.

GRFs++ also generalize how walk lengths are chosen. Instead of relying only on fixed-probability stopping rules, they allow broader distributions over walk lengths. The authors report improved graph-kernel approximation accuracy from this flexibility without extra computational cost. Empirical evaluations and theoretical analysis support both contributions: more efficient access to long-walk information and more flexible control over the walks used for approximation.
icml-2026-computationally-efficient-grap.tldr: GRFs++ approximate graph kernels more efficiently by stitching short random walks and allowing more flexible walk-length distributions.

paragraphs: Negative guidance steers a text-to-image diffusion model away from unwanted content by subtracting a direction associated with a negative prompt. A fixed strength can create a difficult balance: excessive guidance damages image quality or changes the intended prompt, while insufficient guidance can fail against adversarial prompts. The paper proposes adapting this strength to the evolving generation.

Concept Removal Guidance, or CRG, estimates the presence of an unwanted concept at each diffusion step using the model's own noise predictions. It then applies a closed-form constrained update that targets a specified presence threshold while minimizing changes to the conditional generation trajectory. The threshold therefore governs the estimated concept presence used by the update.

CRG needs no additional training, fine-tuning, or external classifier. Across red-teaming benchmarks, the authors report lower attack success while preserving fidelity on benign inputs. They also apply it to artist-style and violence suppression. These findings support using evidence from the current denoising process to calibrate intervention, rather than applying the same removal strength throughout generation.
icml-2026-concept-removal-guidance-evide.tldr: CRG adapts diffusion guidance to estimated unwanted-concept presence, reducing attack success while preserving benign image fidelity in reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Sparse autoencoders break a language model's internal activations into interpretable features that can be amplified to influence behavior. CorrSteer identifies useful steering features from activations observed during generation. Its aim is to automate this process without the contrastive datasets or large stored activation collections required by existing approaches.

The method separates candidate discovery from causal testing. It first finds features whose activations correlate with successful outcomes, then intervenes by amplifying them. Only features that also improve performance under intervention are retained. Steering coefficients come from average activations on correct samples, removing the need for task-specific tuning. Streaming correlation keeps memory use constant with respect to dataset size.

Evaluations on Gemma-2 2B and LLaMA-3.1 8B report gains of 3.3% on MMLU and 27.1% on HarmBench, with lower side-effect ratios than fine-tuning at comparable accuracy. Selected features form interpretable groups, including structured-output, refusal, and domain-semantic features. The pipeline handles hundreds of thousands of features without backward passes or activation storage, connecting interpretable interventions with a scalable selection procedure.
icml-2026-corrsteer-generation-time-llm-.tldr: CorrSteer automatically selects language-model steering features through outcome correlation followed by intervention tests, without storing activations or using backward passes.

paragraphs: Instruction tuning on diverse tasks faces two problems: updates from different datasets can conflict, and coordinating distributed training consumes communication bandwidth. MERIT tackles both by dividing a training mixture into partitions, training those partitions independently, and combining their weights once. The partitioning is explicitly informed by estimated conflicts between dataset gradients.

The theoretical motivation uses a local quadratic approximation within a shared flat basin. Under that setting, merging reduces curvature-weighted variance, and splitting along principal conflict directions maximizes the gain in high-curvature directions. The analysis also describes merging as spectral filtering with implicit norm regularization. MERIT turns these results into a pipeline using PCA-based conflict partitioning and token-weighted averaging, with no communication between partitions during fine-tuning.

On Qwen2.5-VL-3B trained with 136 Vision-FLAN tasks, the eight-benchmark average rises from 54.3 under joint training to 57.0. The recipe also matches or exceeds centralized training for a 7B model on a larger mixture, with minimal cost overhead, and transfers to text-only FLAN. These results support independent training followed by a carefully prepared merge.
icml-2026-decentralized-instruction-tuni.tldr: MERIT partitions instruction data by gradient conflict, trains independently, and merges once to improve evaluated performance while avoiding inter-partition training communication.

paragraphs: Language models increasingly evaluate other systems, but inspecting their individual judgments gives limited insight into whether they behave as reliable measurement instruments. This paper shifts the focus from isolated outputs to the properties of the judge itself. It proposes a two-phase diagnostic framework grounded in Item Response Theory and its Graded Response Model.

The framework separates reliability into two complementary dimensions. Intrinsic consistency asks whether the judge's measurement behavior remains stable when its prompt changes. Human alignment asks whether its assessments correspond to human evaluations of quality. Keeping these dimensions separate makes the diagnosis more informative: stability under prompt variation and correspondence with people are distinct questions that an evaluation procedure needs to examine.

The authors apply the framework to seven language-model judges and report interpretable signals for systematically diagnosing their judgments. These signals are intended to help verify reliability and identify potential sources of unreliable behavior. The contribution is a structured way to investigate how a judge measures quality, extending validation beyond simply observing the scores it produces.
icml-2026-diagnosing-the-reliability-of-.tldr: An Item Response Theory framework diagnoses language-model judges through prompt stability and alignment with human quality assessments.

paragraphs: A reusable robotic skill can become unusable when the robot's body or environment changes, even if the intended task stays the same. Adapting the skill is especially difficult in dynamic, partially observed environments where large language models are unavailable. RECENT addresses this setting by making the adaptation task more manageable for small language models.

The framework represents skills as executable code and separates their semantic intent from the execution bindings tied to a particular body or environment. It preserves the control structure expressing what the skill should accomplish, then performs localized refactoring of the bindings needed to execute it. This focuses adaptation on the incompatible parts rather than asking the model to regenerate the entire program.

The authors evaluate multiple robot embodiments and skill-grounding scenarios in dynamic environments. RECENT delivers robust long-horizon performance with a small language model, achieves the strongest results among the evaluated small-model Code-as-Policies methods across all scenarios, and matches the task performance of large-model Code-as-Policies. The findings support preserving existing skill structure as a useful aid to efficient adaptation.
icml-2026-efficient-skill-grounding-via-.tldr: RECENT enables small language models to adapt robotic skills by refactoring execution bindings while preserving the skills' existing control structure.

paragraphs: Physical risk depends on both a scene and what an agent plans to do in it. Systems without explicit action-conditioned risk reasoning can overlook dangerous interactions or flag too many harmless ones. EMBGuard separates this reasoning from the agent's policy, providing a dedicated safety guardrail for evaluating proposed actions in their visual context.

Given a visual observation and an action, EMBGuard identifies hazardous configurations and explains potential risks in natural language. The work also introduces EMBHazard, with 15.1 thousand training pairs, and EMBGuardTest, containing 329 manually curated real-world scenarios across seven physical-risk categories. Varying combinations of hazards and actions supplies both risky and benign cases that may arise during planning.

The authors report that compact 2B and 4B versions achieve performance competitive with proprietary multimodal models while significantly reducing false-positive rates. That result matters because excessive warnings can interfere with real-time use as well as useful action selection. The evaluation supports action-conditioned hazard assessment as a distinct component of embodied planning, with explanations accompanying its risk judgments.
icml-2026-embguard-constructing-hazard-a.tldr: EMBGuard evaluates visual observation–action pairs to explain physical hazards, achieving competitive risk assessment with fewer false positives in compact models.

paragraphs: Synthetic training examples can help models become more robust and generalize better, but generating clinical text introduces a specific concern: altered or invented medical information can make an example misleading. This paper develops an augmentation framework intended to preserve the critical clinical content while still benefiting from a language model's ability to generate text.

The proposed framework uses query-based collaboration between models to bring expert-level domain knowledge into the generation process. That knowledge guides augmentation toward medically faithful examples. Its central design choice is to make domain guidance part of producing the augmented data, connecting the flexibility of text generation with the need to retain information that matters for clinical interpretation.

Compared with both existing language-model augmentation and traditional augmentation methods, the authors report significantly better preservation of critical medical information and fewer hallucinations at the token and concept levels. Downstream clinical prediction experiments also show consistent performance gains. Together, these findings support the lightweight collaborative approach as a way to improve both the faithfulness and practical training value of synthetic clinical text.
icml-2026-expert-guided-clinical-text-au.tldr: Query-based model collaboration guides clinical text augmentation with expert knowledge, improving medical-information preservation and downstream prediction in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Graph networks can struggle under heterophily, where connected nodes need not have similar properties. The paper identifies a mechanism in repeated neighbor aggregation: components aligned with a node's own representation can become reinforced while signals with inconsistent phases are suppressed. GESC changes how neighbor messages are processed to reduce this self-reinforcement.

GESC uses complex-valued representations and transports messages consistently under U(1) phase transformations. For each transported neighbor message, it removes the component parallel to the target node's representation before computing attention. A sign-aware gate then uses complex alignment that is invariant to these transformations. This design combines consistent handling of phase with explicit cancellation of self-parallel message content.

The authors prove that the hidden update is gauge-equivariant and derive stability bounds with coefficients held fixed, showing contraction of self-parallel message components. On nine benchmarks, GESC ranks first on seven and in the top three on the remaining two. These results suggest that cancelling this specific component can improve message passing under heterophily, alongside the stated symmetry and conditional stability results.
icml-2026-gauge-equivariant-graph-networ.tldr: GESC improves evaluated heterophilous graph learning by cancelling self-parallel neighbor-message components within a gauge-equivariant complex-valued network.

paragraphs: Some decisions can proceed only when every stakeholder considers the outcome acceptable by their own minimum standard. This paper studies whether randomizing over a finite set of options can satisfy everyone. The algorithm proposes lotteries over those options and receives binary accept-or-reject feedback, rather than starting with a full description of each stakeholder's requirements.

The authors develop deterministic and randomized algorithms that either find a unanimously acceptable lottery or certify that none exists. Adaptive querying can avoid eliciting many stakeholders' constraints, and randomization further reduces expected elicitation cost compared with collecting everything. The approach therefore makes the amount of consultation needed part of the computational problem, alongside finding a feasible decision.

Worst-case lower bounds establish unavoidable costs, including linear dependence on stakeholder count and logarithmic dependence on precision. Learning-augmented algorithms additionally use advice, such as likely binding stakeholders or a promising lottery, to reduce queries when predictions are accurate while preserving worst-case guarantees. The results distinguish opportunities for efficient elicitation from costs that cannot generally be eliminated.
icml-2026-learning-unanimously-acceptabl.tldr: Query-based algorithms find unanimously acceptable lotteries or certify infeasibility, using adaptivity, randomization, and advice to reduce stakeholder elicitation costs.

paragraphs: Extending a language model's usable context through continued training is expensive because full attention scales quadratically with sequence length. This paper starts from the observation that most tokens can rely on nearby context. Learning To Attend, or L2A, adds a layer that decides separately for each token when access to the entire sequence is needed.

This conditional access makes global attention selective while retaining it where the model calls for long-range information. On Qwen 2.5 and Qwen 3 models, the authors extend effective context from 32 thousand to 128 thousand tokens. L2A stays within 3% of standard long-context training performance while skipping global attention for approximately 80% of tokens and outperforming prior baselines.

Custom Triton kernels translate the token-level decisions into GPU efficiency, with reported improvements of up to about twofold in training throughput and time to first token over FlashAttention. After training, highly sparse global-attention layers can also be pruned, reducing key-value cache memory by up to 50% with negligible performance loss. The results connect selective memory access to both computational and storage savings.
icml-2026-learning-when-to-attend-condit.tldr: L2A learns which tokens need global attention, extending evaluated context length while reducing attention computation and key-value cache memory.

paragraphs: Weight quantization reduces the storage needed to serve language models, but reaching binary or smaller effective representations can demand substantial computation, data, or extra storage. NanoQuant targets this extreme compression regime with a post-training method. It represents full-precision weight matrices through low-rank binary matrices and associated scales, allowing binary and sub-one-bit compression.

The method frames compression as a low-rank binary factorization problem. An alternating direction method of multipliers solver initializes the binary factors and scales, after which block-level and model-level reconstruction tune those parameters. This combines a structured compact representation with a reconstruction process intended to preserve the behavior represented by the original weights.

The authors report a new Pareto frontier for low-memory post-training quantization, meaning an improved trade-off among the evaluated alternatives. Their deployment example compresses Llama-2-70B by 24 times in 13 hours using one H100, enabling the resulting 70B model to run on an 8 GB consumer GPU. The training hardware and deployment hardware serve different roles: the compression computation produces a representation small enough for the latter.
icml-2026-nanoquant-efficient-sub-1-bit-.tldr: NanoQuant uses low-rank binary factorization and reconstruction to compress language-model weights to binary and sub-one-bit representations.

paragraphs: Multivariate forecasting models must learn from variables with temporal dependence, periodicity, and cross-variable correlations. Normalizing or decomposing the input can address aspects of changing data distributions, but these operations do not directly regulate dependence arising among parameters during optimization. This paper examines training itself through a parameter-decorrelation perspective.

The authors model stochastic optimization as a Markov chain in parameter space and use its stochastic differential equation interpretation. Their practical signal is per-step transition variance caused by gradient noise, which reflects optimization-induced dependence and update uncertainty. They observe that this variance can grow during training and theoretically show that such growth can worsen generalization diagnostics.

Transition-variance alignment, or TVA, responds by smoothly adjusting the step size according to the mismatch between an estimated noise scale and a chosen target. It keeps effective transition variance near a prescribed scale without changing the model architecture. Across real-world multivariate forecasting benchmarks, TVA consistently improves accuracy, with negligible overhead and compatibility across diverse methods. The contribution is therefore a training adjustment that complements interventions applied directly to the data.
icml-2026-parameter-decorrelation-via-tr.tldr: TVA improves evaluated multivariate forecasts by adapting optimization step sizes to keep gradient-noise-induced transition variance near a target scale.

paragraphs: Tokenization converts text into the units a language model consumes, making it the first processing step for incoming text. Although tokenizer computation commonly uses simple CPU dictionary lookups, its surrounding system costs can be substantial. Scheduling delays, core selection, copying, and related overhead matter especially for latency-sensitive embedding services, small models, and agentic applications.

PinTok redesigns tokenizer deployment around dedicated CPU and memory resources. It combines core and memory pinning with avoidance of scheduling and context-switch costs, and removes duplicate network-packet copying and processing. The approach targets the machinery surrounding tokenization, treating resource placement and data movement as central parts of tokenizer performance.

The implementation can replace existing tokenizer deployments directly. Reported latency reductions reach up to 95% for average latency, 97% at P50, 94% at P90, and 87% at P99; throughput improvements reach up to 2,084%. These are upper-end reported improvements rather than uniform gains. The findings show that optimizing a seemingly lightweight preprocessing stage can produce substantial tokenizer-level efficiency benefits by reducing system overhead.
icml-2026-pintok-tokenizers-deserve-dedi.tldr: PinTok accelerates tokenizer serving by pinning CPU and memory resources and removing redundant scheduling, copying, and network-processing overhead.

paragraphs: This paper studies sampling from distributions specified by unnormalized densities, combining learned samplers with particle-based methods. A learned sampler can reuse what training has taught it, while sequential Monte Carlo maintains and updates a collection of candidate samples. The proposed approach connects these methods through maximum-entropy reinforcement learning.

In this connection, the learned sampling policy supplies proposal kernels, while value functions supply twist functions that guide sequential Monte Carlo. Samples generated by this particle procedure then train the neural sampler through off-policy reinforcement learning. Because the procedure itself uses the learned sampler as its proposal, the two components form a training loop intended to improve exploration of the target distribution.

The authors introduce techniques for stable joint training, adaptive weight tempering to reduce training-signal variance, and a replay-buffer method combining historical samples with annealed importance weights. Tests cover synthetic multimodal targets in continuous and discrete spaces and alanine dipeptide conformations. Compared with both amortized and Monte Carlo methods, the approach improves approximation of the target distribution and training stability in these evaluations.
icml-2026-reinforced-sequential-monte-ca.tldr: A reinforcement-learning and sequential-Monte-Carlo training loop improves learned sampling accuracy and stability on evaluated multimodal and molecular distributions.

paragraphs: Applying policy-gradient reinforcement learning to diffusion and flow models is difficult because their likelihoods are intractable. Existing methods often emphasize new optimization objectives while using likelihood estimates whose effects receive less attention. This paper separates three design choices: the policy-gradient objective, the likelihood estimator, and the procedure used to sample rollouts.

The analysis identifies an evidence-lower-bound likelihood estimator, calculated using only the final generated sample, as the dominant factor in effective, efficient, and stable optimization. Across the studied reward tasks with SD 3.5 Medium, the estimator matters more than the particular policy-gradient loss. This shifts attention toward how the algorithm estimates likelihood when interpreting the success of an RL training recipe.

The reported method raises GenEval performance from 0.24 to 0.95 in 90 GPU hours. The authors report 4.6 times greater efficiency than FlowGRPO and twice the efficiency of DiffusionNFT, without reward hacking. Consistent trends across the evaluated tasks support the likelihood-estimation finding within this experimental setting, while the factorized analysis clarifies which design component drives the observed gains.
icml-2026-rethinking-the-design-space-of.tldr: The study finds that ELBO-based likelihood estimation matters more than policy-gradient loss choice for efficient diffusion-model RL in its evaluations.

paragraphs: Vision-language-action models connect visual observations and language to robotic control. Methods that improve them at inference time can require additional training, verifiers, or repeated forward passes. The paper also identifies a perceptual limitation: changing action decoding alone leaves the visual representation fixed, even when uncertainty arises from ambiguity in what the robot sees.

SCALE uses the model's self-uncertainty to adjust both perception and action during inference. When uncertainty is high, it broadens exploration in both; when the model is confident, it favors exploitation. Inspired by uncertainty-driven exploration in Active Inference, this strategy makes how the model looks part of the same adaptation process as how it acts.

The method requires no extra training or verifier and operates in a single forward pass. Evaluations on simulated and real-world benchmarks show improvements to state-of-the-art vision-language-action models and better performance than existing test-time scaling methods while retaining single-pass efficiency. The stated findings support joint perception-and-action adaptation as a practical way to respond to varying conditions without the repeated computation required by those alternatives.
icml-2026-scale-self-uncertainty-conditi.tldr: SCALE uses self-uncertainty to adapt both visual perception and robotic action in one forward pass, without additional training or a verifier.

paragraphs: Many specialized language and multimodal models descend from the same foundational language model. This paper investigates whether those family relationships preserve internal behavior relevant to contextual truthfulness. It assigns attention heads context-truthfulness scores and compares those scores across foundational models and their instruction-tuned or multimodally adapted descendants.

Across Vicuna-, Qwen2.5-, LLaMA2-, and Mistral-based families, the authors find strong preservation of these scores. That inheritance is consistent with preservation of attention-head weights, and heads with strong contextual-truthfulness scores attend to evidence relevant to the query. The findings connect model lineage with a measurable internal tendency to use supplied context.

TruthProbe builds on this pattern through soft gating: it amplifies context-truthful heads while retaining contributions from other heads. The method improves contextual truthfulness on HaluEval and reduces multimodal hallucination on POPE and CHAIR. Scores obtained from base language models also transfer effectively to their descendants. This suggests that measurements made on a foundational model can guide useful interventions in related specialized models, as demonstrated in the evaluated families.
icml-2026-the-truth-stays-in-the-family-.tldr: TruthProbe amplifies context-truthful attention heads whose scores persist across model families, improving contextual truthfulness and reducing evaluated multimodal hallucinations.

paragraphs: Retrieval-augmented generation can be manipulated by poisoned passages inserted into the retrieved context, even when relatively few passages are corrupted. This paper examines whether those attacks can also remain inconspicuous. It formalizes stealth through a distinguishability-based security game and argues that a few passages controlling the response must exert disproportionate influence on inference.

The defense looks for that influence in the language model's intermediate attention signals. The authors introduce a Normalized Passage Attention Score and a lightweight Attention-Variance Filter that flags anomalous passages. Attention weights serve as an approximation of how strongly different passages affect the response, translating the stealth analysis into a practical detection mechanism.

The method improves robustness, reporting accuracy gains of up to 20% over baseline defenses. The authors also construct adaptive attacks designed to conceal the anomalies, reaching success rates of up to 35%. These attacks show that the defense does not eliminate poisoning, while the combined results expose a useful tension between controlling a response and hiding the influence used to control it.
icml-2026-through-the-stealth-lens-atten.tldr: Attention-based passage scoring detects influential RAG poisoning and improves robustness, though adaptive attacks retain reported success.

paragraphs: Multimodal learning combines information from different input types, often by encoding their signals into a fixed representation. S3 instead organizes that information into semantic experts that can be selected according to the task. The aim is to give the representation an internal structure whose components can be used selectively.

The framework has three connected stages. Specialization creates concept-level experts in a shared latent space. Selection determines which experts should contribute for a particular task. Sparsification then removes low-utility paths, producing compact representations with less retained information. These stages make the organization and routing of semantic components part of the learning approach, rather than treating the final embedding as a single fixed package.

Across four MultiBench benchmarks, S3 improves accuracy and shows a consistent reverse-U relationship between sparsity and performance. Intermediate sparsity performs best, so the observed benefit does not increase indefinitely as more paths are removed. The findings suggest that selectively retaining useful semantic components offers a practical alternative to contrastive or information-maximization-driven approaches to multimodal representation learning.
icml-2026-toward-structural-multimodal-r.tldr: S3 structures multimodal representations into selectable semantic experts, with evaluated performance peaking at intermediate levels of sparsity.

paragraphs: Language-model agents can iteratively improve CUDA kernels by planning from feedback, but it is difficult to determine which feedback actually drives their planning decisions. Removing a feedback source in an end-to-end experiment also changes later iterations. Those diverging trajectories can obscure the effect of the feedback component the experiment intended to isolate.

CUDAnalyst provides a controlled analysis layer that freezes trajectories and selectively injects feedback at individual generations. This supports stable generation-level comparisons and coalitional-style attribution, examining both feedback components and their interactions. The approach is designed to separate immediate feedback-to-plan effects from the downstream drift caused by earlier changes in an iterative process.

The authors find that explicit planning is beneficial only when feedback is aligned, and that effective planning depends on structured interactions among multiple feedback signals. High-level plans from stronger reasoning models also partially transfer to weaker models. These trends hold across the studied backbones, workloads, and induction regimes. Their scope is the controlled axes examined, giving evidence about planning structure without claiming universal behavior across all agents.
icml-2026-towards-feedback-to-plan-decis.tldr: CUDAnalyst isolates feedback effects in CUDA-generation agents, finding that useful planning depends on aligned feedback and structured interactions among signals.
